hook.line: Hernando's prescription says one pill three times a day, and he has opinions about it. English uses *a*, *by* and *for* for all of this. Spanish picks *por* or *para* each time, and the choice changes the meaning.
hook.es: Lo tomas tres veces por día.
hook.en: You take it three times a day. (to a friend)

examples.es: Lo tomas tres veces por día.
examples.en: You take it three times a day. (to a friend)
I exchanged it for another one.

examples.es: Para ser lunes, hay mucha gente.
examples.en: For a Monday, there are a lot of people.
I work eight hours a day.
I send the prescription by mail.

rule:
You already know *para* as a goal or a deadline, and *por* as a reason, a route or a price. Here are the next uses.

*por* is also:
*how often*: *tres veces por día*, *una vez por semana*
*the way you do it*: *por teléfono*, *por correo*
*a swap*: *lo cambié por otro*, trading one thing for another

*para* is also:
*in my view*: *Para mí, es grave*
*measured against what you'd expect*: *Para ser lunes, hay mucha gente*

So ask yourself: is it a rate, a means or an exchange? *por*. Is it an opinion, or a comparison with a standard? *para*.
smallPrint: Teachers call this *para* the opinion or comparison use, and *por* here the frequency, means and exchange uses.

options: In my opinion, it's serious.
Because of me, it's serious.
It's serious, so I can pay.

readAndPick.es: Lo tomo dos veces por día.
options: I take it two times for the day.
I take it twice a day.
I take it twice through the day.
I exchanged it for another one.
I changed it to wait for another one.
I changed it because of another one.

readAndPick.es: Para ser lunes, hay mucha gente.
options: Because it's Monday, there are a lot of people.
To be Monday, there are a lot of people.
For a Monday, there are a lot of people.
I'll call you to get a phone.
I'll call you on the phone.
I'll call you for the phone.

readAndPick.es: Para Vale, el café es lo más importante.
options: In Vale's view, coffee is the most important thing.
Coffee is the most important thing for Vale's sake.
Coffee is the most important thing because of Vale.

readAndPick.es: Cambio el tinto por un jugo.
options: I'm changing the black coffee because of a juice.
I'm swapping the black coffee for a juice.
I'm changing the black coffee to make a juice.

readAndPick.es: Tengo clase dos veces por semana.
options: I have class twice a week.
I have class in order to have two weeks.
I have class for two weeks.

readAndPick.es: Para ser doctor, es muy joven.
options: To become a doctor, he is very young.
For a doctor, he is very young.
Because he is a doctor, he is very young.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose the right word and type the whole sentence: *Lo tomas tres veces ___ día.* (*por* or *para*) You take it three times a day. (to a friend)
yourTurn.answer: Lo tomas tres veces por día.
yourTurn.why: How often is a rate, so *por*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose the right word and type the whole sentence: *___ mí, es muy caro.* (*Por* or *Para*) For me, it's very expensive.
Type in Spanish: We talk on the phone.
yourTurn.why: The way you talk is a means, so *por*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I exchanged the black coffee for a juice.
yourTurn.answer: Cambié el tinto por un jugo.
accept: Cambié mi tinto por un jugo.
yourTurn.why: Trading one thing for another is *por*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: For a Monday, the café is quiet.
yourTurn.answer: Para ser lunes, el café está tranquilo.
accept: Para ser lunes el café está tranquilo.
yourTurn.why: Comparing with what you'd expect is *para ser*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about once a week: *Tengo clase dos veces por semana.*
yourTurn.answer: Tengo clase una vez por semana.
yourTurn.why: The rate stays with *por*, only the number changes.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it a question for a friend: *Para mí, es importante.* Ask whether it's important to him.
yourTurn.why: *Para mí* becomes *para ti* when you ask your friend.

pitfalls.wrong: Lo tomas tres veces para día.
pitfalls.right: Lo tomas tres veces por día.
pitfalls.why: Almost. A rate such as "three times a day" is always *por*.
*Por mí* means "for my sake" or "I don't mind"; to give your opinion of something, say *para mí*.
When you swap one thing for another, English says *for* but Spanish says *por*.
The way you do something (phone, mail) is *por*.

personal: Tell us how often you do something good for you (*dos veces por semana*), or what is serious or important *para ti*.
